junction.name: Atlantic Avenue & Logan Street, New York City

claims.text: Atlantic Avenue & Logan Street had 84 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 11 pedestrians injured, 7 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $5.8 million a year.
34% of crashes here had only people in vehicles hurt, against 24% at the city's priority junctions.

Held up on later years: a vehicle was going straight ahead, heading west in 35% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 18% at the city's priority junctions (found by the AI analyst and the greedy search and the exhaustive search).
Held up on later years: only people in vehicles hurt and it happened in the daytime in 26% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 15% at the city's priority junctions (found by the greedy search).

This corner got turn traffic calming in 2021. Across the city: a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program. Repeating it here is not supported by the city's own record.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).
Leading Pedestrian Interval would avoid about 0.3 crashes a year (CMF 9918, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the city's own past installs passed the causal gate), worth $98,000 a year.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 2.5 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $863,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for Atlantic Avenue, Logan Street (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 37, New York City Council; Brooklyn Community Board 5.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 37, New York City Council; Brooklyn Community Board 5
Subject: Request for safety study and fixes at Atlantic Avenue & Logan Street

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

For the 5 years from 31 October 2021 at Atlantic Avenue & Logan Street, the official record shows 195 crashes, including 84 injury crashes. Eleven pedestrians and 7 cyclists were injured and no one was killed. The city lists this as a priority location.

Using the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), the harm is about $5.8 million per year. No safety work is recorded in this period; the last recorded project was turn traffic calming in 2021.

This corner got turn traffic calming in 2021. Across the city: a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program. Repeating it here is not supported by the city's own record. Please take a different approach.

We ask you to study this junction and, on the roads you own — Atlantic Avenue and Logan Street — consider:

* a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green), expected to prevent about 0.3 pedestrian injury crashes per year (about $98,000 in harm avoided per year). Where the city installed it at 1,651 intersections, pedestrian injury crashes fell 17% (95% interval 11% to 22%) compared with intersections that got it later; a stricter check against fake programs is less certain.
* longer yellow signal times, expected to prevent about 4.6 injury crashes per year (about $1,565,000 in harm avoided per year), after checking on site for an entry on yellow or red.

Please let us know the outcome of the study and next steps.

Sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]

Sources:
- NYC Open Data, Motor Vehicle Collisions - Crashes (h9gi-nx95)
- NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (corridors); NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (intersections); NYC Vision Zero View, Enhanced Crossings (6ax4-q5k4); NYC Vision Zero View, Leading Pedestrian Interval Signals; NYC Vision Zero View, Signal Timing/25 MPH Retiming; NYC Vision Zero View, Speed Humps (jknp-skuy); NYC Vision Zero View, Turn Traffic Calming; NYC Vision Zero priority corridors; NYC Vision Zero priority intersections
- FHWA CMF Clearinghouse, CMF 9918 (a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green))
- FHWA CMF Clearinghouse, CMF 4215 (longer yellow signal times)
- U.S. DOT Benefit-Cost Analysis Guidance, 2026 Update, Table A-1 (2024 dollars)
- NearMissLens NML-Bench T11: before/after study of the city's own installs (validation/BENCH.md)
- Road owners: the registry's road-inventory layer (see the engineer report's receipts)
